title: TACOS: Topology-Aware Collective Algorithm Synthesizer for Distributed Machine Learning
problem: Distributed ML clusters face communication overhead constraints; existing collective communication libraries use fixed algorithms that don't adapt to heterogeneous and asymmetric network topologies. Manually designing collective algorithms for all topology and pattern combinations requires prohibitive engineering effort.
motivation: Efficient network resource utilization is critical for large-scale ML clusters where communication overhead often becomes the performance bottleneck.
method: TACOS automatically designs communication algorithms customized to each cluster's specific network layout and communication patterns. Instead of using generic algorithms that work the same for all systems, it analyzes how the computers are connected (network topology) and what data needs to flow between them, then synthesizes an optimized algorithm for that exact configuration. The key advantage is that the design process itself is polynomial time—meaning it stays computationally feasible even for massive systems—rather than NP-hard approaches that become prohibitively slow at that scale, enabling practical scaling to systems with tens of thousands of processors.
key_novelty: It automatically creates communication algorithms tailored to each specific network layout using polynomial-time computation, making customization practical for systems with tens of thousands of processors.
contributions: Autonomous synthesizer that automatically generates topology-aware collective algorithms for specific patterns and topologies
4.27× performance improvement over state-of-the-art synthesizers on a 128-NPU system
Polynomial-time synthesis enabling scalability to 40K NPUs in 2.52 hours versus NP-hard methods limited to tens of NPUs
Practical synthesis speed of 1.08 seconds for 128-NPU All-Reduce optimization
